clean_body: [ ]Adam Schiff for Senate Derek — The science is clear — we need to take bold action to mitigate the worst impacts of climate change and protect our planet, public lands, and the environment. Donald Trump’s environmental agenda is dangerous, irresponsible, and reckless. Trump not only can’t bring himself to admit that climate change is real, he’s actively making it worse every single day. Donald Trump’s plan for the environment is to make it as easy as possible for polluters, fossil fuel companies, and toxic waste dumpers to make our air dirtier and water unclean. In his very first week in office, he signed executive orders to... Remove the United States from the Paris Climate Agreement Expand oil and gas drilling Weaken the Endangered Species Act Put in place nominees who are beholden to fossil fuel Make it harder for Americans to purchase electric vehicles End protections for poor and minority communities who have disproportionately shouldered the consequences of pollution Derek, I’ve been working on this issue my entire career. After law school, I went to work for the United States Attorney’s Office as an Assistant U.S. Attorney. During my six years there, I fought to hold polluters and toxic waste dumpers accountable for irresponsible environmental practices. My work there even led to the creation of the first federal environmental crimes unit in Los Angeles. My work for the environment continued as a member of the California State Senate and later a member of the U.S. House. I led the way in expanding Metro light rail across Southern California, helped establish California’s earthquake early warning system, and championed legislation to preserve and protect California’s natural beauty and public lands. Now, I’m serving on the Environment and Public Works Committee as a United States Senator. Right now, the current administration is downright hostile to any attempts to protect our environment. And making it worse every single day. But this is a fight worth having — because frankly, we don’t have any other choice. Strong climate action isn’t just good for our environment — it’s good for our economy, too. That’s why I’ve supported the Green New Deal so that we can build a green economy that will create millions of new jobs, lower energy prices for working families, make American energy independent, and dramatically expand clean energy technologies. I can promise you that, as I’ve done my entire career, I will continue to oppose oil and gas drilling off the coast of California, vote against any efforts that weaken environmental protections, and advocate in the strongest terms possible for bold action to tackle climate change and grow our economy. subject: For anyone who loves great literature
body:
C.S. Lewis and J.R.R. Tolkien wrote some of the twentieth century’s most beloved works of literature, including robust defenses of the Christian faith.

This sponsored message from Your American News is on behalf of Hillsdale College

| | | [](https://e.youramerica.news/rd/9z2zphvskigmis02g1lulh41k26efa85h63m4qgsfjo_rp22sh2s8i6eob2clg6apj4cdh2bs)
---
| | Dear Friend,

C.S. Lewis and J.R.R. Tolkien wrote some of the twentieth century's most beloved works of literature, including robust defenses of the Christian faith.

Today, I want to share an exclusive and free video series with you that considers Lewis and Tolkien in the context of their membership in the Inklings--an informal professor-student literary group at Oxford in the 1930s and 40s.

**You can receive instant access to this free video series about the Inklings by using this secure link now:**

**[https://info.hillsdale.edu/the-inklings-cca](https://e.youramerica.news/rd/9z2zfschlas9a8ng7n6fqvlo3stpamvri20kj9g0v3g_rp22sh2s8i6eob2clg6apj4cdh2bs)**

C.S. Lewis is best known for his Narnia books--such as _The Lion, the Witch, and the Wardrobe_ --and his apologetics, including _Mere Christianity_. Indeed, Lewis is one of the greatest Christian apologists of all time.

J.R.R. Tolkien's most renowned works are _The Hobbit_ and _The Lord of the Rings _trilogy.

That both were men of genius is indisputable. Both men also devoted countless hours to honing their craft. This included subjecting their writing to the scrutiny of their fellow Inklings, who met regularly for conversation and to read aloud from and discuss their current work.

**The Inklings are a fascinating topic of study, which is why we 've created a free online video series for you to enjoy. **

The video series, titled "The Inklings," was filmed on the Hillsdale College campus. It examines the ideas that bound the Inklings, what they accomplished, and the continuing importance of their works today--with a special focus on Lewis and Tolkien.

**You can use the secure link below to receive instant access to "The Inklings" free video series:**

**[https://info.hillsdale.edu/the-inklings-cca](https://e.youramerica.news/rd/9z2zn37tjj204qucangcbbdla6ag18344nicblqub3g_rp22sh2s8i6eob2clg6apj4cdh2bs)**

Lewis and Tolkien thought the Inklings' meetings contributed significantly to their literary success. As models of civil discussion and intelligent debate, they stand in stark contrast to today's "cancel culture."

The Inklings, are therefore, worth studying not only for their great literary achievements but also because they exemplify the free speech that is essential to the pursuit of truth.

That's why Hillsdale College created a free online video series on the Inklings. I hope you'll use the secure link above and start watching it today.

Warm regards,

Larry P. Arnn
President, Hillsdale College
Pursuing Truth and Defending Liberty Since 1844

P.S. C.S. Lewis and J.R.R. Tolkien met regularly with an informal literary group named the Inklings.

Now, you can examine the philosophical, theological, and literary ideas that bound the Inklings together with a free video series from Hillsdale College.

**You can receive instant access to this free video series about the Inklings using this secure link:**

**[https://info.hillsdale.edu/the-inklings-cca](https://e.youramerica.news/rd/9z2zvg3lk093piqdvmb5d2ergbhie3ocona3cs8hmo0_rp22sh2s8i6eob2clg6apj4cdh2bs)**

Truth is a fragile thing--without warriors to defend it, it withers.

**Let 's show Project Veritas they can't end me or our mission**. [**Give today, and let 's bury this attack once and for all**](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zdv3tn75td6nf7vq9pa5pn5mt39tr41oj6jjkqog_rp22sh2s8i6eob2clg6apj4cdh2bs).

| | Hi Friend,
---
It might be cliche to say in March as we see all the college hoops action, but the madness of this month and the past 59 days in Washington is real. I wanted to share an update directly from me on what we’re seeing and how I’m fighting for us.
---
From Wall Street to Main Street, Americans are experiencing chaos, confusion, and challenges because of Donald Trump and Elon Musk’s actions. We’ve seen a focus on culture war issues and an assault on government functions but no work by Republicans to address Americans’ high cost of living.
---
Even worse, Republicans in Congress are sprinting towards massive cuts to health care for people in our communities so billionaires receive a massive tax giveaway.
---
I’ve been fighting back by educating people about the real impacts these choices have had on our neighbors, agitating in public forums, supporting the leaders litigating in our courts, and legislating to get our opponents on the record for standing against the American people. I’m on this journey for the long haul.
---
**I try not to bother you with too many emails, but[I am asking for your help to keep up this essential work.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/104196962/534607703/570291875?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDU0NTUiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiYjZkNDA1OWItYjAwNS1mMDExLTkwY2QtMDAyMjQ4MmE5ZmI3IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=z-jKa-p_da-JLLnzFXmhpJ6ZTuVD6h-t2T0wllPEfnA=)**
---
Your contributions enable me to focus on the work of holding Trump and House Republicans accountable. We must do everything possible to lower costs, prevent cuts to health care, and make clear that there is a better way.
---
[**DONATE**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/104196963/534607704/570291875?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDU0NTUiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiYjZkNDA1OWItYjAwNS1mMDExLTkwY2QtMDAyMjQ4MmE5ZmI3IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=z-jKa-p_da-JLLnzFXmhpJ6ZTuVD6h-t2T0wllPEfnA=)
---
I greatly appreciate your commitment to ensuring we stay strong in these heavy times. I remain hopeful and determined to have a brighter future. Please know that your support can help us secure a Democratic leadership in Washington that listens – and focuses on the needs of our people.
---
Let’s keep working together,Gabe

I won’t mince words, Peter: These last few months have been tough.

Los Angeles County was devastated by the worst wildfires in its history and faces a long road to recovery. The Trump administration has dealt blow after blow to our country and democracy.

Thousands of jobs slashed, retirement accounts decimated, economic instability, Social Security threatened – the list goes on.

But, there is hope. I’ve never seen more people engaged in our political process and ready to get to work than right now – even from my time on the campaign trail. Thousands of people are being ignited to take action.

# [](https://act.robbonta.com/go/3?refcode=em20250320&t=1&akid=1702%2E1088799%2E8sroue)
The Attorney General just secured another **endorsement from a major civil rights and human rights organization, Equality California!**
[](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rb-email-20250320?refcode=em20250320-1702&refcode2=1702_1088799_8sroue&akid=1702%2E1088799%2E8sroue)
Equality California is the nation’s largest statewide LGBTQ+ civil rights organization. In a statement, they highlighted Rob’s longstanding commitment to the LGBTQ+ community and further explained why they’re endorsing him for re-election:
_“Since his time in the California Assembly, Rob Bonta has been a fierce advocate for LGBTQ+ people. He has repeatedly demonstrated his commitment to protecting marginalized people against political and legal attacks. As Attorney General, Bonta has used the power of his office to enforce California’s laws that guarantee equal access to education, healthcare, and employment. That is why we fully support Bonta for another term as California's Attorney General. We are confident that he will continue to serve as a strong ally to our community and defend the rights and dignity of all Californians in the face of divisive policies.”_ \- Tony Hoang, Executive Director of Equality California
---
As Attorney General, Rob has fought back against efforts from other states and the Trump administration that seek to erode fundamental protections for the LGBTQ+ community. He has also ensured that California's nation-leading legal protections are enforced across the state.
From protecting LGBTQ+ children and youth from discriminatory and harmful forced outing policies to defending access to gender-affirming care, **Rob is a steadfast ally for the LGBTQ+ community and will continue to be** — especially as the far-right federal administration and Congress and right-wing state legislatures across the country ramp up their bigoted attacks on LGBTQ+ rights.

subject: What is our purpose?
body:
Please see a special message from our sponsor:

Unsubscribe

Please see a special message from our sponsor:

http://trk.victorymailings.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=stfqg4&__onlt=t

Dear Fellow American,

I am enclosing a survey on a very urgent matter.

It will only take a moment of your time, but the topic is vital to our nation's future.

A movement is growing, led by progressives—but supported by many well-meaning Americans—to change the way we elect our president. In effect, it seeks to do away with the Electoral College as devised by the Framers of our Constitution.

That's why Hillsdale College is conducting a National Survey on Presidential Selection.

By completing this survey and returning it to me as soon as possible, you will help Hillsdale College more clearly understand the views of mainstream Americans concerning this issue—views we will make available to policymakers and opinion leaders.

You can complete the National Survey on Presidential Selection by using the link below:

http://trk.victorymailings.com/?xtl=17x64w94u6dj8w52r4g318wr0p69dvq1ouud0m139opmyxnv3n255r085ynji5vp2r2owyvcw4q6y6mmiehqrlsgpx5027b5hzeqd60elarmwmaw0sn0rjknj8i5x71gnxcbl33t2x9bealocwnquzuz8zx9bj&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=stfqg4&__onlt=t
http://trk.victorymailings.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=stfqg4&__onlt=t

Do you think that most Americans understand how the Electoral College works and its role in preserving free and representative government?

YES
http://trk.victorymailings.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=stfqg4&__onlt=t

NO
http://trk.victorymailings.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=stfqg4&__onlt=t

For most of our nation's history, the Electoral College, as devised by the Framers of our Constitution, was not controversial. Indeed, it was considered essential to preserving free and representative government.

But today, more than a dozen states have joined together in an attempt to undermine this constitutional bulwark of liberty.

This movement to undermine the Constitution has grown largely because of the failure of America's schools to provide young people with a proper grounding in American civics—too many Americans simply don't understand the importance of the Constitution, including the Electoral College, to liberty.

Because of this, Hillsdale College has expanded its educational mission on behalf of liberty nationwide, directly teaching millions of Americans in all 50 states.

These efforts, which aim to counter the Left's domination over most of our schools, include:

Teaching millions of citizens nationwide through free online courses, such as "Constitution 101" and "The Great American Story: A Land of Hope;"

Reaching over six million households and businesses nationwide with Imprimis, Hillsdale's free digest of liberty;

Promoting constitutional education through social media outlets popular with young people;

Sending millions of pocket-size copies of America's founding documents to citizens and K-12 schools across America; and

Restoring excellence to K-12 education by helping establish and guiding classical K-12 schools nationwide and providing, free of charge, Hillsdale's American classical K-12 curriculum (including American civics) to thousands of American educators and homeschoolers.

Your answers to the National Survey on Presidential Selection will help Hillsdale form the most effective strategy to educate millions of Americans about the importance of the Constitution to liberty—including the importance of the Electoral College.

And this is especially important in this critical time for America's future.

So please share your views on this urgent topic by completing our National Survey on Presidential Selection and returning it to me as soon as possible. It will only take a few minutes of your time.

You can take the survey using this secure link I've provided below:

http://trk.victorymailings.com/?xtl=17x64w94u6dj8w52r4g318wr0p69dvq1oxqplyoaym7sxv36zl7qapvjqric28la8guvjt94ejan29s3inj0chnkovo9kibnmpc7qxp1disnm0mrb4uei5bi73ber7ql7ljzafhmzijy49tnxdg5k0vhl65ntt&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=stfqg4&__onlt=t
http://trk.victorymailings.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=stfqg4&__onlt=t

And after you take your survey, I hope you will also consider supporting Hillsdale College with a tax-deductible gift.

Since 1844, Hillsdale has been "pursuing truth and defending liberty." Today, it does so through its extensive educational outreach efforts while refusing to accept ONE PENNY of government funding—not even indirectly in the form of federal or state student grants or loans.

The support of private citizens like you is essential to our work.

Please represent your state and take the National Survey on Presidential Selection today. Thank you for your time and attention—and for your friendship and support of liberty.

Warm regards,

Larry P. Arnn

President, Hillsdale College

Pursuing Truth and Defending Liberty Since 1844

body:
Honesty. Accountability. Leadership. It shouldn’t be rare.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20250320-1&t=1&akid=1879%2E587540%2ELkvlVw)
Peter,
It’s refreshing to see some goddamn leadership.
**At a recent town hall stop, Governor Tim Walz said he is doing some “soul searching” about Democrats’ loss in 2024.**
He admitted that many voters didn’t see a difference between Kamala Harris and Donald Trump — and the one big reason for that is because voters think Democrats in power are too timid about taking action to improve peoples’ lives.
Governor Walz didn’t dodge, deflect, or sugarcoat. He did what too many Democrats refuse to do: **take accountability, be honest with people, and focus on actually doing better.**
**_We need more of that._**
After the election, I took a hard look at my role.
When I met with President Biden, I should have pushed harder. I should have said what needed to be said — that the voters wanted Biden to step aside far earlier than he did — even if speaking that truth made people uncomfortable.
Too many Democrats played it safe when we should have been listening to young voters, organizing harder, and preparing for the fight ahead.
We can’t afford to make the same mistakes again.
That’s why Leaders We Deserve is working to elect young, unapologetic progressives who get it — **leaders who know what’s at stake, listen to their constituents, and have the guts to lead with honesty.**
The establishment won’t change on its own. We have to compel it.

subject: Our rights and freedoms in Wisconsin depend on you, Peter
body:
This race is going to be close, and the stakes are high. |
---
[](https://click.everyaction.com/k/104205707/534629928/-92542179?refcode=WUEFH349_20250320_CrawfordBaldwin_ALL_v1s1&sourceid=1055863&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9UU00vVFNNRUwvMS84NzA2OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJiOTFlZmZlNi1iZTA1LWYwMTEtOTBjZC0wMDIyNDgyYTlmYjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=5qRMgOqUWJPdSszvIiyIyqsE19d48OUPddSKP2r6d5g=) Peter,

I'm no stranger to how close statewide races in Wisconsin can be. Last fall, my race was the most expensive Senate race our state has ever seen — and it all came down to just a few votes. **This year, the stakes are just as high.**

**Right now, right-wing special interests are pouring millions into Wisconsin to try to buy a seat on our Supreme Court. And now, Elon Musk has weighed in — making it clear that the far right is all-in on flipping control of the court.**

_We can't let them win._ We have a chance to elect Judge Susan Crawford, a dedicated public servant who will protect our rights and uphold the law. But with the GOP's megadonors opening their checkbooks, we have to fight back with everything we've got. [**Can you split a donation between Susan Crawford's campaign and EMILYs List? Your support is critical if we want Susan to win this race.**](https://click.everyaction.com/k/104205708/534629929/-92542179?refcode=WUEFH349_20250320_CrawfordBaldwin_ALL_v1s1&sourceid=1055863&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9UU00vVFNNRUwvMS84NzA2OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJiOTFlZmZlNi1iZTA1LWYwMTEtOTBjZC0wMDIyNDgyYTlmYjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=5qRMgOqUWJPdSszvIiyIyqsE19d48OUPddSKP2r6d5g=) | [SPLIT A DONATION](https://click.everyaction.com/k/104205709/534629930/-92542179?refcode=WUEFH349_20250320_CrawfordBaldwin_ALL_v1s1&sourceid=1055863&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9UU00vVFNNRUwvMS84NzA2OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJiOTFlZmZlNi1iZTA1LWYwMTEtOTBjZC0wMDIyNDgyYTlmYjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=5qRMgOqUWJPdSszvIiyIyqsE19d48OUPddSKP2r6d5g=)

clean_body: This race is going to be close, and the stakes are high. | = Peter, I'm no stranger to how close statewide races in Wisconsin can be. Last fall, my race was the most expensive Senate race our state has ever seen — and it all came down to just a few votes. This year, the stakes are just as high. Right now, right-wing special interests are pouring millions into Wisconsin to try to buy a seat on our Supreme Court. And now, Elon Musk has weighed in — making it clear that the far right is all-in on flipping control of the court. We can't let them win. We have a chance to elect Judge Susan Crawford, a dedicated public servant who will protect our rights and uphold the law. But with the GOP's megadonors opening their checkbooks, we have to fight back with everything we've got. = | = Reproductive rights, funding for public education, voting rights, and so much more is on the line in this race. It's already clear that this will not only be one of the closest races in the country, but it will also be the biggest race of 2025 — and we know that every dollar makes a difference. Happy Persian New Year, Peter! Today is a time to celebrate new life and new beginnings as spring begins. In fact, the Persian New Year, “Nowruz,” literally translates to “new day” in Farsi. Growing up, I looked forward to celebrating Nowruz with my family. My mom would set the “Haft Sin” table, and we’d visit friends and family for two weeks of festivities. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/104207072/534632935/1386712341?refcode=AU_YA_CL_GEN_GEN_AC_20250320_PM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS83OTA5NyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhMzcyOWVhMC1jMDA1LWYwMTEtOTBjZC0wMDIyNDgyYTlmYjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=G_Z1yJ5CzjePYAIVStwehy2K2qagS5OzBpj2dmvGWXU=) The Persian New Year meant so much to me growing up, but I didn’t see leaders in my community talking about the holiday as much as other events. That’s why I had the idea of bringing the first-ever Nowruz celebration to Phoenix City Hall as a Councilwoman! Not only did I want to share this experience with people all across Arizona, but I also wanted to show the hundreds of Afghan refugees fleeing the Taliban who made Phoenix their new home that our city is welcoming and inclusive to all. **Peter, what better way to do that than by bringing this beautiful, multicultural celebration to the heart of our city!** Thousands of residents showed up to this year’s celebration to make sure immigrants and refugees feel welcome here. I couldn’t be prouder of Arizona for making this happen. As we celebrate Nowruz this year and in years to come, let us remember that brighter days are ahead, and that we must all work together toward a shared future of peace, prosperity, and mutual understanding. My mom would set the “Haft Sin” table, and we’d visit friends and family for two weeks of festivities. = The Persian New Year meant so much to me growing up, but I didn’t see leaders in my community talking about the holiday as much as other events. That’s why I had the idea of bringing the first-ever Nowruz celebration to Phoenix City Hall as a Councilwoman! Not only did I want to share this experience with people all across Arizona, but I also wanted to show the hundreds of Afghan refugees fleeing the Taliban who made Phoenix their new home that our city is welcoming and inclusive to all. Peter, what better way to do that than by bringing this beautiful, multicultural celebration to the heart of our city! Thousands of residents showed up to this year’s celebration to make sure immigrants and refugees feel welcome here. I couldn’t be prouder of Arizona for making this happen. As we celebrate Nowruz this year and in years to come, let us remember that brighter days are ahead, and that we must all work together toward a shared future of peace, prosperity, and mutual understanding. Thank you, Yassamin | = Yassamin Ansari for Congress PO Box 13524 Phoenix, AZ 85002 United States | mailto:info@yassaminforcongress.com | Paid for by Yassamin Ansari for Congress.

[](http://trk.victorymailings.com/?xtl=muyxrsrigog0w6rfcwv4ynz3c6j91q4swuwdxwmixun66wbnsbkrgimltl0457o0ic5qyrx81j2lykzlpyhepkalktptxq3wfa0hhrb1cudbt1jmq932am6gfp9jepoczc313e555nvhwb26w8ue9l3ge4kxb5xdgl8vkn04wgbz2k3vuyw6sol53zaopz0rtewzjfrbyba9j3kwyudk8t5o70olza26yskn3m99yg23n7gozobl8poozg6jhsxfw6txaxjedvxupysbwps&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=stftif&__onlt=h)
Friend,

I wanted to take a few minutes today to tell you a little bit about myself, my life story, and what's never going to change.
**__My Upbringing__**
I was raised in Zachary, Louisiana where I was taught the values I live by today by my mother and father. Those same values that I fight for each and every single day to protect. Values like hard work, dedication, and putting God and family first in everything.
[](http://trk.victorymailings.com/?xtl=muyxrsrigog0w6rfcwv4ynz3c6j91q4swv5bmfx1qpbnyolmik7cv7ubsu3z0a9xajp01yi43blcjr16olq6scutujxxecng3chhh2h7sfgdl5tcgm87emrtgg2mvvzbxzjc2qlx7qp1j9t8qmhdn58obtpjfpbyf1q7iy6fnf9tugvnncxernl9mb45134ltezwcfjdnrxmgf3za9ckdqpuu3egkr40nztdvknzyqjkx2cmxwjgn77t32pgxgygweps7z1nbza8ro9uefo&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=stftif&__onlt=h)
After high school, I attended Vanderbilt University, graduated, and then went on to receive my law degree at the University of Virginia. I tell you that so you know that I know a little more about law than the average pink-haired woker would like you to believe.
**__So, what'd I do after college?__**
I was elected to five terms as State Treasurer where I managed the state's $10.6 billion investment portfolios. I also oversaw local and state bond issues and returned millions of dollars in unclaimed property each year. Before I was Treasurer, I served as Secretary of the Department of Revenue, Special Counsel to Governor Roemer, and Secretary of Governor Roemer's Cabinet.

For too long, our education system has been under attack by political agendas that seek to dismantle the support structures our students need to succeed. Yet when given the chance to protect girls' and women's sports, he voted to let men take over. The fact is, Democrats care more about a woke agenda than fairness, safety and opportunity for female athletes. As a former NCAA swimmer, I know firsthand what it feels like to have the sport I love stolen by men who were allowed to compete against women. It's unfair, it's dangerous and it must stop. clean_body: They had a choice—stand with female athletes or cave to the woke mob. In 2026, we’ll make them pay. | Fellow Patriot - I'm furious, and I know you are too. EVERY. SINGLE. SENATE. DEMOCRAT. had a choice: stand up for female athletes or cave to the radical left. They chose to abandon women. This includes vulnerable far-left Senator Jon Ossoff who has a daughter. Yet when given the chance to protect girls' and women's sports, he voted to let men take over. The fact is, Democrats care more about a woke agenda than fairness, safety and opportunity for female athletes. As a former NCAA swimmer, I know firsthand what it feels like to have the sport I love stolen by men who were allowed to compete against women. It's unfair, it's dangerous and it must stop. The Senate is red. Republicans fought for this bill. But without a filibuster -proof majority, the radical Left still has the power to kill commonsense legislation like this. That's why I'm fighting to unseat EVERY Democrat who voted against protecting women's sports. I can't do this alone. The Democrats have made their choice. Now, it's our turn. Let's fight back. **“A group funded by Elon Musk is behind deceptive ads in crucial Wisconsin Supreme Court race”**
— _Associated Press_ Peter, The Wisconsin Supreme Court election in two weeks is one of the biggest battleground elections of 2025 — and early voting just started _Tuesday_. Here’s why this race is so important: In the years to come, the court could determine the fate of critical issues like the fate of gerrymandered maps, voting rights, abortion rights, and more. We’ve endorsed Democracy Defender Judge Susan Crawford — a fair and impartial public servant who has fought for our rights. But she’s up against Brad Schimel — “an outspoken supporter of Mr. Trump” who “has echoed Mr. Trump’s lies about elections,” according to _The New York Times_ , and who’s in favor of the state’s 1849 abortion ban. She’s also facing the full strength of the GOP as a group funded by Elon Musk pours millions into the race and targets voters with deceptive attack ads — the same misleading strategy they used to help elect Trump. **It’s clear: the far right is going all out to try to flip this seat and take back control of the Wisconsin Supreme Court. We can’t let them.** **In the final stretch of this high-stakes race, we’re on the razor’s edge between democracy and extremism. Peter, Elon Musk recently suggested that the United States privatize the U.S. Postal Service. Here’s Becca’s response: **No. ** Privatizing the USPS would have _devastating_ consequences for millions of folks in Vermont and across the country — especially seniors, veterans, small business owners, and people who live in rural communities. Prices would skyrocket. Deliveries of critical items like checks and life-saving prescription drugs would slow down. And mail-in voting — one of the most popular voting methods nationwide — would be at risk. Let’s be clear, Peter — **this is a blatant attempt by Donald Trump and Elon Musk to dismantle one of our country’s most essential public services.** **[Becca refuses to sit quietly and let them sell the USPS off to the highest bidder. name: Mandela Barnes
subject: A very sad day for our nation and future generations
disclaimer_text: Paid for by The Long Run PAC, P
body:
Trump just ordered the dismantling of the Department of Education.
#
[](https://act.mandelabarnes.com/signup/doe_em_march25/?source=em250320-1-240&akid=5504%2E196590%2E23UgpS)
Team — I’m struggling for words right now.
Trump just ordered the dismantling and eventual shutdown of the Department of Education.
**This is a staggering blow to our nation and the future we are leaving behind for generations to come.**
The Department of Education was created to strengthen public education in this country and ensure that every student from every background has a shot at a quality education that can put them on the path to prosperity and success.
This devastating decision by the Trump administration will raise class sizes, cut job training programs, make higher education more expensive, take away special education services for students with disabilities, and gut student civil rights protections.
And of course, this move is about gutting public education as much as it’s about paying for more tax breaks for billionaires like Elon Musk, too.
When the president oversteps his mandate like Trump did today, the job falls to Congress to correct course.
Congress has the power to protect the Department of Education **_right now_** by overriding Trump’s executive order with legislation.
That’s why I’m asking you today: [**Sign our petition calling on Congress to take action to protect the Department of Education. Let’s show members of Congress that the American people will not stand for this outrageous and disastrous move by Trump.**](https://act.mandelabarnes.com/signup/doe_em_march25/?source=em250320-1-240&akid=5504%2E196590%2E23UgpS)
[ADD YOUR NAME](https://act.mandelabarnes.com/signup/doe_em_march25/?source=em250320-1-240&akid=5504%2E196590%2E23UgpS)
I hope you’ll join me in taking this simple but important action to show that Americans are outraged by Trump’s attacks on public education.
— Mandela Barnes

President Trump lives in a fantasy if he thinks closing the Department of Education is a good idea.
It’s a terrible idea!
Americans know that the key to achieving the American dream begins with a good education.
The Education Department provides support for K-12 schools all around the country. It helps students pursuing higher education and job training programs with financial aid. It allows students with disabilities to access the same education opportunities as other students. And so much more.
Gutting the Department of Education would harm every single student across America. It would have negative consequences for our country’s economic growth and our competitiveness for decades to come. And it would set America’s students up for failure.
I won’t just stand by while Trump destroys America’s future. Add your name to my petition to demand the protection of the Department of Education. [https://secure.ngpvan.com/BMcgxjV9bU2028I66Le5sA2]
There is nothing more important right now to our nation’s success than making sure students get the high-quality education they need — and I will use every legislative tool at my disposal to fight this absurd shutdown.
Thanks for speaking up — more updates to come as we take action.
-Tim Kaine

subject: Together, We Can Protect Virginia's Future
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY GARY MILLER FOR DELEGATE121 Bell Ct
body:
This election isn't about a president, it is about the hard working people of Virginia.

| | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/a181279422a8/together-we-can-protect-virginias-future?e=606d7e9aa2)
---
| | | | |

[](https://drmillerforyou.us9.list-manage.com/track/click?u=db0c834d5d03c9893fbbb1d8a&id=8a65397e98&e=606d7e9aa2)
| **Friend,**
This week I submitted 261 petitions, more than **twice the number** required to officially secure my place on the ballot for the House of Delegates. I am deeply humbled by this moment. Each signature **represents a person** who believes in our campaign, our community, and the future we can build together.
This election **isn't about** Washington, D.C., **a president** , or even a political party. It's about the **hard working and often overlooked** people of Southside Virginia and our entire Commonwealth. It's about fighting for:
* **Good-paying jobs** that sustain our families.

* **Fully funded public schools** that prepare our children for the future.

* **Affordable healthcare** that ensures no one is left behind.

* **Protecting our hospitals and small businesses** , which are the lifeblood of our communities.

Recent federal decisions have led to significant cuts in essential services, placing a **heavier burden** on our state legislature to **fill the gaps**. These challenges affect every corner of Virginia, making **each seat in the House of Delegates crucial** in our fight to safeguard our shared values and future.
That’s why I’m running for the House of Delegates. This seat has been Republican for 24 years, but with new district lines, **we only need 5% to flip it.** We can win, but only if we have the resources to fight back.
[**Can I count on you to donate today?**](https://drmillerforyou.us9.list-manage.com/track/click?u=db0c834d5d03c9893fbbb1d8a&id=296e8ffc8f&e=606d7e9aa2) Every dollar goes toward reaching voters, fighting for our schools, and ensuring Virginia steps up where Washington is failing.

Peter,

Last week, I joined my colleagues in Congress to reintroduce the Credit for Caring Act, a bipartisan bill that would create a new tax credit of up to $5,000 for working family caregivers.

Since 1979, the Department of Education has been at the forefront of supporting students and educators across the country. The Department protects the civil rights of students, ensures our students with special education needs have the resources they deserve, provides professional development for educators, manages student loan programs, and makes sure that students in low income communities have access to a high quality public education.
All of that work is in jeopardy: Just moments ago, Trump signed an executive order to dismantle the Education Department.
This is **unconstitutional. Congress created the Department of Education,_so only an act of Congress can dissolve it_.**
This attempt by the administration to unilaterally dismantle the Department of Education and so many other government agencies is an extreme overreach and completely rejects the balance of power.
Children across the country depend on the support the Department of Education provides and public education should not be a trade off to provide tax breaks to the wealthiest among us.
**We must fight back against this illegal attack from the Trump administration.**

Hi Peter, our people-powered movement has grown _so much_ in the last few months — so I wanted to take a moment to reintroduce myself.

Growing up in public housing in the Bronx, raised by a single mother making minimum wage, I learned a strong work ethic and strong values that **continue to guide and inspire me everyday.**

I learned firsthand the importance of social safety nets, because those were a lifeline for my family. I learned how _critical_ it is to invest in affordable housing. I learned, from a young age, that working class families are often overlooked in Washington — and I vowed to change that.

**Now, thanks to the grassroots support of people like you, I’m in Congress, doing just that.**

Meanwhile, I’m watching as Trump and Elon Musk do _everything they can_ to make an enemy of working class people in America. They want to line _their_ pockets while the rest of us lose access to Social Security, Medicare, SNAP benefits, and more.

**But Peter, from public housing in the Bronx to the halls of Congress, I know firsthand that the _only way_ to overcome something is to face it head on. And that’s exactly what we’re going to do.**

name: Pramila Jayapal
subject: Will you sign on to my petition calling for a constitutional amendment to overturn Citizens United?
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Pramila for Congress
body:
Over the last three weeks we’ve seen the consequences of billionaires being allowed to spend unlimited amounts of money to tip an election.
# [](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/892?refcode=em20250320-4869-footer&t=1&akid=4869%2E420207%2ER-uAgQ)
Peter,
Since Donald Trump’s second term began, we’ve seen the consequences of billionaires being allowed to spend unlimited amounts of money to decide an election.
Elon Musk spent more than $290 million on the 2024 election, and now Donald Trump is allowing him to dismantle our government and sell it for parts — all so billionaires like him can pay even less in taxes than they already do.
**We need to return power to the people — which is why last month, I reintroduced a constitutional amendment to overturn the _Citizens United_ decision that has wrought havoc on our political system in the first place.**
[**If you’re with me in this fight, will you sign on to my petition calling for a constitutional amendment to overturn _Citizens United_ today?**](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/signup/em20250320-citizens-united-petition?source=em20250320-4869&akid=4869%2E420207%2ER-uAgQ)
The second Trump administration may be taking it to a new level, but the truth is our democracy has been left vulnerable to the influence of wealthy billionaires, special interests, and corrupt Super PACs all the way since the Supreme Court’s flawed decision back in 2010.
The next time Democrats are in power, we can’t just talk the talk. We need to walk the walk and finally take action to end the corrupting influence of Big Money in our politics.
**But in order to get this done, it’s going to take a mass nationwide movement of working people who are fed up with the status quo.**
[**Peter, if you’re on board, will you add your name to my petition to demand Congress overturn _Citizens United_ and finally return power to the people?**](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/signup/em20250320-citizens-united-petition?source=em20250320-4869&akid=4869%2E420207%2ER-uAgQ)
**[Sign Your Name](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/signup/em20250320-citizens-united-petition?source=em20250320-4869&akid=4869%2E420207%2ER-uAgQ)**
In solidarity,
Pramila Jayapal

body:
Our children deserve better.

[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/104218429/534653450/1806897946?refcode=EM_F_250320edu_N_SB_90DO_5_NG_N_logo&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjEvMS84Nzg0NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJiNjU5Yjk3YS1kMjA1LWYwMTEtOTBjZC0wMDIyNDgyYTlmYjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=wDsNCe8ieVtDPY1-BQgV9wy5IdCttpFOEgHVo0g7mr4=) **Peter – Trump has signed an executive order directing Education Secretary Linda McMahon to SHUT DOWN the department.**

Trump is attempting to once again play king by directing Sec. McMahon to take all necessary steps to close down the Department of Education and return education authority to the States. This also comes on the heels of the Ohio legislature passing the horrific Senate Bill 1, which would strip away worker rights and micromanage what can be taught in the classroom at colleges and universities – including setting rules around electoral politics, DEI, foreign policy, immigration, and more.

**I am disgusted by these ridiculous attacks by Trump and his fellow Republicans, who aim to dismantle our democracy and strip away opportunity for children.**

name: Travis Tazelaar, VoteVets
subject: Ira Hayes
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY VOTEVETS, VOTEVETS
body:
The people who serve — no matter their gender or race— have earned our recognition and respect. But this administration is far more interested in erasing their legacies than building upon it.
#
Peter, this is Travis with VoteVets. I’m a Marine Corps Veteran, and I want to tell you about a fellow Marine — Ira Hayes.
He was born in 1923 to a father who served in World War I. He was raised on Arizona’s Gila River Reservation just southeast of Phoenix, and was a member of the Pima Tribe. Things were tough for Ira growing up. Money was short, and there wasn’t much opportunity.
In 1942, at 19, he enlisted in the Marine Corps. Ira was a good Marine. In 1943 he sailed to the Pacific Theater and fought in the Bougainville campaign for the better part of 11 months. Bougainville was tough, but nothing like what came next.
In February of 1945 he was one of 70,000 Marines who landed on the beaches of Iwo Jima, a small, volcanic island several hundred miles south of Japan. The battle of Iwo Jima is one of the most storied in the history of the Marine Corps, and for good reason. Of the 82 Medals of Honor awarded to Marines, more than 25% of them are from Iwo.
Ira fought on Iwo Jima for 36 days until the island was secured. A few days into the battle, Ira climbed Mount Suribachi alongside several of his comrades. When they reached the top, they took part in the second flag raising over Iwo Jima — and you’ve probably seen the picture:
[](https://act.votevets.org/signup/250320_vv_em_ira_hayes/?source=em250320-1-90&akid=34266%2E3013755%2EEoYAOz)
We suffered nearly 30,000 casualties in the 36 days before Iwo Jima was secured, and more than 6,500 dead. Of the six men who raised that flag, three were killed in action by the time the battle was over. Ira’s platoon had 45 men when they landed on Iwo, and of that number just 5 were left at battle’s end.
Ira was identified as one of the flagraisers, and by then the photo from Iwo Jima was already one of the most famous in American history. He was pulled into an immensely successful War Bond tour that raised $26 billion (roughly $450 billion today). When the war ended, he was honorably discharged and returned home to Arizona.
The war took a heavy toll on Ira. Everyone up to the President of the United States called him a national hero for his service during the war. But Ira never felt like he was any more important than the other guys he fought beside, or the friends he lost in combat. In spite of his fame, he struggled to hold down work. And, like many veterans before and since, he suffered from alcoholism and Post Traumatic Stress Disorder.
Ira Hayes died in January of 1955, just a few weeks after he helped dedicate the Marine Corps War Memorial in Arlington. Ira’s story, to me, is one worth telling. To me, Ira is a hero.
But the Trump Administration would have us forget him. They’ve deleted government webpages about Ira. They’ve done the same to far too many others, like Jackie Robinson, the Tuskegee Airmen, the Navajo Code Talkers, and thousands more.
They’re doing this because of a misguided campaign to eradicate so-called “DEI” from the government and the military. “Diversity” is dead, according to Pete Hegseth’s Pentagon. On Monday, his spokesperson said, “I think the president and the secretary have been very clear on this — that anybody that says in the Department of Defense that diversity is our strength is, is frankly, incorrect.”
The people who serve — no matter their gender or race— have earned our recognition and respect. But this administration is far more interested in erasing their legacies than building upon them.
I’m not going to stand for it.
Peter, we’re asking for your help. [**Join VoteVets in demanding that the Trump Administration and the Department of Defense stop whitewashing our shared history, and restore these pages. This is the least we can do to honor them.**](https://act.votevets.org/signup/250320_vv_em_ira_hayes/?source=em250320-1-90&akid=34266%2E3013755%2EEoYAOz)
| [ADD YOUR NAME](https://act.votevets.org/signup/250320_vv_em_ira_hayes/?source=em250320-1-90&akid=34266%2E3013755%2EEoYAOz)
---
With everything happening right now, this might seem like a small act to take. But we project our values through the history we observe and the heroes we honor. People like Ira Hayes sacrificed a lot for us and for our country.
VoteVets will not let Trump erase them.
Thank you,
Travis
Travis Tazelaar
Political Director, VoteVets
Marine Corps Veteran

| | Last week, I voted **against** advancing and passing the Republican-penned, hyper-partisan bill to fund the government. I had a choice here: support a bill that gave Donald Trump and Elon Musk a blank check to continue their dismantling of federal agencies and firing of federal workers, or advocate for a _truly clean_ bill to fund the government for several more weeks and buy us more time to negotiate for clear restraints on executive branch overreach. **I chose to stand with the millions of concerned Americans who want Congress to reassert its authority and put a check on an out-of-control President.** While I'm deeply disappointed that the Republican bill passed – setting the stage for a broader budget fight in September – I come away from last week all the more determined to keep fighting. I just held four open-to-all town halls in Oregon and one with the Oregon delegation and Oregon's Attorney General for current or recently-fired federal workers who have lost their jobs as a result of Trump and Musk's dangerous cuts. And my takeaway is that our movement is equally determined to fight back. The days and weeks ahead will not be easy, but I know our movement has what it takes to push back. The door has opened even further now for Republicans to pass devastating cuts to Medicaid, Social Security, food assistance, and countless other programs that Americans benefit from. **In the months ahead, we must harness the energy of our grassroots movement and empower people to speak out against the dangers of the GOP's plans.** We must continue to encourage folks to call their members of Congress and attend town halls – or demand their members hold town halls at all. We must keep highlighting the damage caused by Trump's and Musk's rampage through federal programs. When our voices rise together, _no one can shut them out._ Because nobody voted for an unelected foreign billionaire to take total control of our government and cut off the services that millions of families rely on. There is no one single lever we can pull to suddenly stop Trump, Musk, and their allies in Congress, but we can make every day count. I chose to stand with the millions of concerned Americans who want Congress to reassert its authority and put a check on an out-of-control President. While I'm deeply disappointed that the Republican bill passed – setting the stage for a broader budget fight in September – I come away from last week all the more determined to keep fighting. I just held four open-to-all town halls in Oregon and one with the Oregon delegation and Oregon's Attorney General for current or recently-fired federal workers who have lost their jobs as a result of Trump and Musk's dangerous cuts. And my takeaway is that our movement is equally determined to fight back. The days and weeks ahead will not be easy, but I know our movement has what it takes to push back. The door has opened even further now for Republicans to pass devastating cuts to Medicaid, Social Security, food assistance, and countless other programs that Americans benefit from. In the months ahead, we must harness the energy of our grassroots movement and empower people to speak out against the dangers of the GOP's plans. We must continue to encourage folks to call their members of Congress and attend town halls – or demand their members hold town halls at all. We must keep highlighting the damage caused by Trump's and Musk's rampage through federal programs. When our voices rise together, no one can shut them out. Because nobody voted for an unelected foreign billionaire to take total control of our government and cut off the services that millions of families rely on. There is no one single lever we can pull to suddenly stop Trump, Musk, and their allies in Congress, but we can make every day count. We can reclaim the narrative, block the GOP's grand legislative plans, and lay the groundwork – slowly but surely – for electing bold Democrats across the country in 2026 who understand the stakes of this moment and will stand for the people. Derek,
When Donald Trump was running in 2016, there were at least _some_ Republican elected officials willing to speak out against him.
This time around, all the Republican politicians have fallen into line. That’s emboldened Trump and made him even more dangerous.
What that means for us is that we need to be even more vigilant, and we need to push back twice as hard.
**Democrats are not going to win in 2026 by rolling over today. We can’t wait two years to show some backbone.**
We need to be a party of fighters, showing the American people that we are standing up for them. We need to sharpen our message and better connect with voters.
That’s the way to win, and it’s the right thing to do.
If we believe—and I do—that Donald Trump and his MAGA allies are a threat to our freedoms, our well-being, and our entire economy, then now is the time to step up, speak out, and get loud.

* **TOP NEWS**

"**Justice Department moves to drop lawsuit that would allow Texas police to arrest migrants** ," AP's **Nadia Lathan** -- "The Trump administration has moved to dismiss a Biden-era lawsuit against Texas over a state law that would allow local police to arrest migrants who enter the country illegally, days after the administration's decision to [dismiss similar lawsuits](https://substack.com/redirect/55c249bc-951b-4aed-9a75-e576168ebe85?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) against Iowa and Oklahoma.

The Justice Department under the [Biden administration had sued Texas](https://substack.com/redirect/c2039c16-cc89-40ed-96ed-9f74630cb3e2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) over concerns that the law, known as Senate Bill 4, was unconstitutional and sought to supersede federal authority.

Signed by Republican Gov. **Greg Abbott** in 2023, the law would allow law enforcement to arrest migrants for illegal entry and give judges the authority to order them to leave the country. It took effect for just a few hours last year before a federal appeals court put it on hold.

Abbott signed the bill to challenge the federal government after accusing the Biden administration of failing to enact immigration enforcement.
[BECOME A PAID SUBSCRIBER: $7/mo](https://substack.com/redirect/81cc81ae-8c47-4dc2-a41e-18c87c91c00f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The Trump administration's decision shadows its refusal to pursue lawsuits against [Iowa](https://substack.com/redirect/3ade3cb1-d017-41b3-bffa-2d73535a1c14?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and [Oklahoma](https://substack.com/redirect/93bea2ff-bb7d-44dc-baac-7a3cb884e5b5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), which enacted similar state immigration laws to allow state and local officials to arrest and charge immigrants in the U.S. illegally.

Texas' law has been considered the most far-encompassing by legal experts and opponents, allowing police anywhere to carry out immigration enforcement.
[BECOME A PAID SUBSCRIBER: $70/yr](https://substack.com/redirect/81cc81ae-8c47-4dc2-a41e-18c87c91c00f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Senate Bill 4 was one of many efforts by Abbott during the Biden administration to instill more state control over immigration enforcement, which has included busing tens of thousands of migrants to Democratic-controlled cities and installing giant buoys in the Rio Grande to deter migrants from crossing the river from Mexico." [AP](https://substack.com/redirect/94200a96-52df-41db-bb51-1a210c0d1bd4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

"**Sam Houston National Forest fire forces 900 evacuations** ," Houston Chronicle's **Sondra Hernandez** , **Octavia Johnson** , **Caroline Wilburn** , **Catherine Dominguez** , **John Lomax V** -- "A large [wildfire at Sam Houston National Forest](https://substack.com/redirect/dda1dd75-48fc-41f0-8759-33222cc1bf49?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) north of the Houston area sparked evacuations and school closures as fire crews worked to contain the nearly 2,400-acre blaze.

Officials warned dry and warm weather conditions would make containing and extinguishing the fire more difficult. Several air tankers, dozers and additional firefighters arrived Thursday to aid in fighting the burn.

"Please say a prayer for all those affected by this fire and for the men and women first responders working to keep us safe," Montgomery County Judge **Mark Keogh** [wrote on Facebook](https://substack.com/redirect/f5bf010a-d513-4652-82ef-4dc167d03ac2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).

The Pauline Road fire had reached 2,360 acres by 2 p.m. Thursday, according to the Texas A&M Forest Service.

The wildfire remained at 20% containment as fire crews continued working to extinguish the burn." [Houston Chronicle](https://substack.com/redirect/1fea849f-1582-44da-9645-9bf9feefc05c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) ($)

"**Rising supply of houses in Central Texas means more choices for would-be buyers** ," Austin American-Statesman's **Shonda Novak** -- "As elevated mortgage rates continue to put a damper on the housing market locally and nationally, rising inventory, slower sales and lower prices have made for more favorable conditions for potential buyers in the Austin-area housing market.
That's according to the latest monthly report from the Austin Board of Realtors.

Home prices declined in the five-county Austin region in February as a growing supply of available homes created more options for buyers, the Austin Board of Realtors said in its February report.

Last month, the median home sales price across the Austin-Round Rock-San Marcos metro area was $430,000, down 3.9% from February 2024, the realtors board said. The median price means half the houses sold for more than that amount, and half for less.

Across the region, sales fell 6.5% year-over-year, with 1,856 homes changing hands. Rising inventory indicates growing opportunities for buyers heading into the spring homebuying season, board officials said in a release.

"While elevated mortgage rates and affordability challenges have factored into the decline in sales, sellers are lowering prices to attract buyers, helping to further stabilize the market," **Clare Knapp** , the board's housing economist, said in a statement.

"As we head into the traditionally busy spring homebuying season, increased options and improved pricing flexibility could encourage more buyers to transition from renting to homeownership," Knapp said.

Inside Austin's city limits, the board reported 674 sales last month, 1.2% fewer than a year ago February. Half of the homes last month sold for more than $564,000 and half sold for less, for a 2.6% increase in the median price.

Before mortgage interest rates started climbing in 2022, home prices in the Austin area had been increasing sharply due to strong demand and insufficient supply, experts said." [AAS](https://substack.com/redirect/a07e9d61-66f1-4c3e-8aa1-a325e23f89a0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) ($)

"**San Antonio Spurs partner is working with Elon Musk's DOGE** ," San Antonio Express-News' **Tom Orsborn** and **Marc Duvoisin** -- "A partner in the San Antonio Spurs is working with **Elon Musk 's** [Department of Government Efficiency](https://substack.com/redirect/8b228c1b-85c9-4303-a4b2-ce454286dd69?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), the unofficial agency that is spearheading mass layoffs of federal employees and deep spending cuts for the Trump administration.

**Joe Gebbia** is the billionaire co-founder of Airbnb and is described as a close friend of Musk's. He is a board member of Tesla Inc., where Musk is CEO.

Gebbia joined the Spurs investor group as a "strategic partner" in January 2022, the NBA franchise said at the time. Last week, he accompanied Texas Gov. **Greg Abbott** to watch the Austin Spurs, a Spurs-owned team that plays in the NBA's developmental league.

A longtime Democrat and major donor to the presidential campaigns of **Hillary Clinton** in 2016 and **Joe Biden** in 2020, Gebbia revealed in January that he had experienced a political reawakening and had voted for **Donald Trump** in November.

Gebbia's political turnabout and his involvement in Musk's DOGE [prompted some Airbnb hosts and guests to threaten to abandon](https://substack.com/redirect/50fd9c46-8edb-4691-8050-ff56cb31b2fe?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the online rental marketplace.

Gebbia, 43, an Austin resident, no longer has an operating role with Airbnb but remains on its board and is a major shareholder. He also is chairman of the nonprofit Airbnb.org, which provides temporary lodging to refugees, asylum seekers and victims of natural disasters.

Airbnb has [sought to distance itself from Gebbia's politics](https://substack.com/redirect/0a2ce244-915d-46e6-bbc7-cdcfd6a022c9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), saying that he is working with DOGE "in his personal capacity" and that his views don't reflect those of Airbnb or Airbnb.org.

[Spurs Sport & Entertainment](https://substack.com/redirect/84d6b859-3349-4402-9634-d629f0eb9d5b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), which owns the Spurs, did not immediately respond to a request for comment." [SAEN](https://substack.com/redirect/f75b9745-b9c4-4dd4-9ce0-7c6217398682?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) ($)
* * *
* **#TXLEGE**

**" Different pace and priorities separate Texas Senate and House on school vouchers**," Texas Tribune's **Jasper Scherer** and**Jaden Edison** -- "The last time the Texas Legislature tried to pass a school voucher program, [nothing seemed to go right](https://substack.com/redirect/94b1e501-4928-4fde-9e25-a659a3c64a7e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for Gov. **Greg Abbott** and his pro-voucher allies.

After months of political threats and last-ditch attempts to salvage Abbott's signature issue, [the demise of vouchers](https://substack.com/redirect/2009f10a-ed34-4b70-96df-187aa9a7b93f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in late 2023 underscored a simple truth: lawmakers couldn't engineer anything that would pass the voucher-resistant House while meeting the standards of Abbott and the Senate.

Two years later, the gulf between the chambers is far narrower as the GOP-controlled Legislature takes another stab at providing taxpayer funds for families to send their kids to private schools. To make [vouchers](https://substack.com/redirect/8780eb34-3873-4303-9c6f-5007314c1d98?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a reality this year, House and Senate lawmakers will have to reconcile differences in their respective bills over how much money students would receive, which applicants would take priority and how the program would accommodate students with disabilities.

Those disparities, though significant, are nowhere near the discord from 2023, voucher supporters and critics agree. Last time, House and Senate negotiators butted heads over formative issues like who would be eligible to participate and what sort of academic accountability standards to impose.

Sen. **Brandon Creighton** , the upper chamber's lead negotiator on vouchers for the second straight session, said it was "very encouraging to see the alignment" between the first drafts of the voucher plans, known as [Senate Bill 2](https://substack.com/redirect/706e915e-0798-4913-ad7f-43b3aeea9096?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and [House Bill 3](https://substack.com/redirect/da60fb6d-4a95-4c13-ac3e-a87618c18de1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).

"There are some distinct differences, but that's always the case," Creighton, R-Conroe, said in an interview. "I was so concerned about vast differences, like I've seen in the past, that when I saw the House version, I was very pleased."

Lt. Gov. **Dan Patrick** , the powerful Senate leader and a fervent voucher supporter, [has also given](https://substack.com/redirect/65fdee2a-f2c1-4096-83ed-50629ea60861?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) his stamp of approval to the House's opening salvo.

Rep. **Brad Buckley** , the Salado Republican who is the House's point person on vouchers, said he had not yet discussed the bill with Patrick but took his comments as a positive first step.

"That's always good, because this process does require both chambers to agree," Buckley told The Texas Tribune. "I think that we've got everything sort of lined up for us to really get some good policy done, make a historic investment in public schools, and then also pass a very strong school choice program."

A [slim majority of the House](https://substack.com/redirect/73041bd3-8162-4a13-b790-ed66e2550cd8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) signed on in support of Buckley's HB 3 last month, the first sign it has enough support to pass. That marked a key milestone for the lower chamber, where past voucher proposals have repeatedly gone to die, thwarted by opposition from Democrats and rural Republicans. Voucher critics say such a program would drain resources from Texas' already struggling public schools, which receive state funding based on student attendance. Supporters say vouchers, or "school choice" programs, would provide alternatives for families who are dissatisfied with their local public schools yet cannot afford to send their kids elsewhere.

Last year, many of the House's GOP holdouts retired or lost their primaries against Abbott-backed candidates who are now among the majority supporting Buckley's bill.

The reconfigured math in the House explains much of the alignment between the two chambers' voucher bills. Many of the biggest differences in 2023 boiled down to Buckley's attempts to win over skeptical lawmakers -- concessions that often proved unpalatable to Abbott, Patrick and Creighton. Among the carrots Buckley offered was [limiting eligibility](https://substack.com/redirect/f5e7ea0b-e873-4c86-8b26-4dbfb4b20036?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to those with a disability, those who qualify for free or reduced lunch, or those who attend low-rated schools; and imposing stricter accountability measures such as kicking students out of the voucher program if they fail a standardized test two years in a row.

Now unfettered by the need to court so many voucher skeptics, Buckley's latest proposal, HB 3, is more expansive than versions rejected by the House two years ago. Both chambers have proposed opening eligibility to virtually any school-aged child and not requiring private schools to administer the state's standardized test -- aligning on two of the biggest sticking points from 2023.

"They're nearly identical, except for some key areas," said**Jaime Puente** , director of economic opportunity at the left-leaning think tank Every Texan, contrasting the situation this year to "the chasm that we saw in the House last time from what the Senate was proposing."

Still, the voucher bills have several hurdles to clear before reaching Abbott's desk -- leaving myriad opportunities for changes that could complicate negotiations or bleed support in the House, where Buckley's bill has only a few votes of breathing room. Creighton acknowledged the potential for "many amendments and changes" to the House's current draft.

While the Senate sprinted out of the gate and in a 19-12 vote [passed SB 2 in early February](https://substack.com/redirect/4ff7583d-de96-45c2-9e88-b405eb86e973?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), the House voucher bill has yet to clear Buckley's Public Education Committee, which [heard more than 22 hours of testimony](https://substack.com/redirect/a6d6ed2e-09f6-425d-b218-036427d28c84?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on the measure last week. Buckley said Wednesday he is working on an updated draft of HB 3 based on feedback from the hearing, along with a new version of the chamber's school funding bill, which House Republicans are moving in tandem with their voucher proposal.

Buckley said he is waiting for updated language from the Texas Legislative Council -- the state agency that drafts bills for lawmakers -- and expects to advance both education bills in "probably a week or two." As for the pending changes to HB 3, Buckley said, "a lot of it's technical, quite frankly."

"I think we will, hopefully, have something that the Senate will feel like is close to what they would like," Buckley said. "That'll be their call, but hopefully we'll be close."" **" Dan Patrick's promise to ban THC could kill a booming $8B industry**," Houston Chronicle's **Tanya Babbar** ,**Isaac Yu** and**Matt Zdun** -- "Never in a million years did **Ann Gauger** think she and her husband would start growing cannabis on their family farm in Lubbock.

After all, the couple grew up in the 1980s, during the era of "Just Say No" and a nationwide war on drugs. Now they operate the largest indoor hemp farm in Texas. Their THC-derived products, including gummies, oils and flowers, help supply some of the [thousands of businesses that have popped up in the state over the last five years](https://substack.com/redirect/994b44f5-a961-407c-958d-7c66b318311b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), since lawmakers in Austin legalized hemp.

The success, Gauger said, has been a lifeline for their family farm amid dropping commodity prices and water shortages in the Panhandle.

Critics in the Legislature say the [booming and largely unregulated market in Texas](https://substack.com/redirect/3e5eb8ea-161d-4eaa-9884-267609cae008?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) has gone too far, and are especially worried that THC gummies are being sold to children. They contend their 2019 farm bill that legalized hemp sales was never meant to allow intoxicating or psychoactive products, and after years of unsuccessfully trying to rein it in, they're opting for a full ban.

"Don't deceive yourself. There's nothing good in this product because you're not able to control it," state Sen. **Charles Perry** , R-Lubbock said while introducing the bill. "It's been exploited for money and profit."

Retailers and farmers say a ban would have devastating consequences for what some estimate to be an $8 billion industry that ranges from smokeshops to high-end restaurants serving cannabis-infused cocktails. They prefer state lawmakers enact new safety regulations, such as age restrictions and product testing requirements.

"It doesn't feel fair to customers, or to people who have invested in this industry to lose it all from a few bad actors," said **Adyson Alvis** , one of the owners of Wild Concepts, a company that owns Grinders, a CBD coffee shop and dispensary, and Wild, a THC bar chain in Houston.

**Jordan Thompson** , a 27-year-old from Houston's Heights neighborhood, said he finds the idea of a THC ban "anti-economy" and fears it will punish Texans.

"A ban is going to put people in a trap for doing what they want in a free country," he said. "Banning THC in Texas will just help the state make money off fines, and citizens will get hurt."

If you feel like cannabis is everywhere, you're not alone.

Smoke shops have become a ubiquitous part of strip malls in cities and suburbs alike, with stores often openly advertising intoxicating products even as the state still criminalizes marijuana.

That's because Texas isn't like other states that have openly ushered in recreational use of the drug.

In 2019, after hemp was legalized at the federal level, Texas lawmakers designed a state statute to boost farming the crop but keep out intoxicating products by banning high levels of delta-9 THC, the element in marijuana that gives users a high. Soon, stores dedicated to selling hemp-derived CBD products, like lotions and oils, popped up all over the state.

But as demand for those products slowed, the oversupply of hemp brought a new product on the market in 2021: a hemp-derived variety of THC known as delta-8 that's not explicitly banned by state law. After a state effort to crack down on the substance failed, consumer demand skyrocketed and businesses started selling the psychoactive products statewide.

Across Texas, the industry generated $8 billion in revenue during 2022, according to a [study](https://substack.com/redirect/c1c690db-d66e-435b-a12f-308debed39a8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by the Whitney Economics Group. The report also estimates a total economic impact of around $20 billion across manufacturing, wholesale and retail, though advocates say the industry has likely expanded significantly since then.

That growth has alarmed lawmakers, Lt. Gov. **Dan Patrick** chief among them.

"In the last two years, 8,000 locations have opened up that are selling above the marijuana limit, sometimes three or four times of the marijuana you would buy on the street from a drug dealer," Patrick, a Republican who leads the state Senate, [said on WFAA](https://substack.com/redirect/ad7b7db1-6001-4380-91fb-f5e6e8284a3b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in January. "It's a billion-dollar industry that has sprung up in 24 months."

Businesses that sell any type of hemp product, from gummies that produce a high to non-psychoactive lotions, need a license from the Department of State Health Services. Farms that grow cannabis are regulated by the Texas Department of Agriculture." "**95,000 Texas children are waiting for state help to pay for day care** ," Texas Tribune's **Jess Huff** -- "Shortly after her eldest son was born in 2021, **Acacia Tarver** applied for a state scholarship to help her pay for child care. Then she waited. And waited.

As time dragged on with no word on aid, Tarver and her husband, **Ty 'Kiedren**, a police officer, discussed who would quit their job to stay at home with their son, Hudson. That July, Tarver put 3-month-old Hudson in a Montessori day care so she could return to work as a surgical coordinator at an insurance company.

The Tarvers learned four months later that they were awarded a scholarship, which is funded by taxpayer dollars. It couldn't come soon enough.

"The day care was sending emails of a tuition increase, and it was increasing by $150 to $200 a month," Tarver said. "Who can afford that? You're basically working to send your child to day care."

Today, nearly 95,000 Texas children are [waiting](https://substack.com/redirect/2287a9b3-5ea7-482d-90c5-9a4f21c96a06?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for similar aid, according to the Texas Workforce Commission. About 1,300 of them live in Deep East Texas communities. Those at the top of the list in Deep East Texas have been waiting for a scholarship since May 2024, officials said.

State lawmakers are considering pumping the scholarship program with more money.

"My goal would be to infuse some dollars to reduce that wait list," said state Rep. **Armando Lucio Walle** , a Houston Democrat. "So many families would like to go to work, but it's just cost prohibitive."

However, child care professionals say that won't help much. Like most of the nation, Texas has a shortage of child care centers and workers. Despite the extraordinarily high tuitions families pay to place their children in day care and after-school programs, those fees are rarely enough to cover the costs of operating these facilities.

That's especially true in Deep East Texas, said **Marilyn Hartsook** , the interim director of Workforce Solutions in Deep East Texas.

"Without new day care centers around the region, we're probably not looking at a whole lot more (children) that we can serve," Hartsook said.

**Charles Miller** , director of health and economic mobility at [Texas 2036](https://substack.com/redirect/0af9b594-e851-4d8d-9b5d-fccdd2434335?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), an Austin-based think tank, said the state needs better data to address its child care deserts and support existing facilities.

"We don't even have the basic insight into where there is a supply gap, and where there is a demand gap," Miller said. "These are core information gaps as we talk about how to intelligently spend and invest state resources."" "**Southwest Airlines cuts back at four more airports** ," Dallas Morning News' **Kyle Arnold** -- "[Southwest Airlines](https://substack.com/redirect/565ea6bb-fd80-4097-91e8-24b30962d8e2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) is cutting employees at four major airports in California and Maryland, the latest belt-tightening in the carrier's ongoing shakeup.

Southwest is in the middle of a series of cutbacks, after activist investor Elliott Management waged a contentious fight over the company's strategies and leadership. The battle [culminated in a board shakeup](https://substack.com/redirect/c39af368-3f40-421f-b3b0-e3e7a72ba45c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and changes to signature Southwest offerings.
